title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.34888v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. translated_title: 新物理搜索中的“观察别处效应”：从经典方法到机器学习
translated_abstract: 当效应在参数空间中的位置未被事先指定时，就会产生“观察别处效应”：扫描许多位置会夸大最大超出量的显著性，因此必须将局部p值修正为全局p值。一个成熟的框架——根植于Davies的工作，并由Gross和Vitells在粒子物理中加以实际应用——为连续参数扫描提供了这种修正。然而，某些方面仍存在争议。“别处”的定义是模糊的，其范围可以从单一分布延伸到整个实验项目。此外，经典框架的解析捷径并不适用于基于机器学习（ML）的搜索，后者受到一种隐式的后选择偏差影响，该偏差取决于模型的分辨率和表达能力。本综述涵盖了对撞机新物理搜索中的LEE，从其统计基础到这些现代挑战。
tldr: 本综述系统回顾了对撞机新物理搜索中的“观察别处效应”（LEE），涵盖基于Davies与Gross-Vitells的经典统计修正框架，并讨论了“别处”定义的模糊性以及机器学习搜索中隐含的后选择偏差等尚未解决的现代挑战。
en_tdlr: This review surveys the look-elsewhere effect (LEE) in collider searches for new physics, covering the classical Davies/Gross-Vitells correction framework and addressing unresolved modern challenges such as the ambiguous definition of "elsewhere" and the implicit post-selection bias affecting machine-learning-based searches.
